answer: An agent market requires every active identity, represented as a vertex in its trading graph, to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding. A public escrow ledger acts as a lantern: anyone can verify that each bidder has funded its own bond. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens; recycling the same funds cannot bypass the lock. A spiral of new identities demands more capital, imposing an opportunity cost even if the bonds are later returned.
